briefings.title: Big Short Reunion w/ Danny Moses: Rising Rates, AI & Private Equity | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 80
briefings.tldr: Former "Big Short" partners Steve Eisman and Danny Moses discuss current market risks, drawing parallels between today's massive AI debt issuance/securitization and the 2008 subprime mortgage warehouse lines, while also analyzing the federal deficit, the housing market, and private equity's growing monetization challenges.

briefings.title: AI Doomsday Fears, Hacking & the Fight for Control with Gary Marcus | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 79
briefings.tldr: AI critic Gary Marcus and host Steve Eisman examine the growing narratives around AI doomsday predictions, recent hacking incidents involving autonomous agents, and whether labs are manufacturing hysteria to shape regulation and secure funding.

briefings.title: Q3 2026 Market Recap: Energy Up, Utilities Crushed, and Software Flipped | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: Steve Eisman delivered his Q3 2026 market recap, noting that energy was the best-performing sector while utilities were crushed, the SaaSpocalypse tech narrative flipped, and over 65% of the S&P 500 has become a single bet on AI.

briefings.title: 5% Rates, Bessent's Failed Gamble & What Comes Next w/ Krishna Guha | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 78
briefings.tldr: Krishna Guha and Steve Eisman break down the rise of the 10-year Treasury yield above 5%, attributing it to a combination of AI debt issuance crowding out Treasuries, war-driven oil prices, a massive 6% GDP deficit, and Kevin Warsh’s removal of Fed forward guidance guardrails.

briefings.title: What the AI Boom Looks Like From Inside Cisco with Sam Badri | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 77
briefings.tldr: Sam Badri, Head of Investor Relations at Cisco, explains that Cisco's revenue growth has accelerated from normalized mid-single digits to 15-18%, driven by a booming hyperscaler AI business and a campus refresh cycle.

briefings.title: Stock Picking in Difficult Times with George Noble | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 76
briefings.tldr: George Noble and Steve Eisman break down current macroeconomic pressures, including Scott Bessent's failed attempts to repress interest rates, the structural risks of the AI capex boom, the unwinding yen carry trade, and massive overvaluations in speculative momentum darlings like Tesla and SpaceX.

briefings.title: Why Dario Amodei and Sam Altman Are Faking the AI Doomsday Crisis | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: Steve Eisman breaks down why Dario Amodei and Sam Altman’s AI extinction warnings are a strategic shell game to invite regulation and build pricing moats, while also covering rate hikes, his FICO short, and portfolio diversification away from AI.

briefings.title: P&C Stocks Worth Owning: The AI Hedge with Ryan Tunis | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 74

people.name: Ryan Tunis
people.role: Property and Casualty Insurance Analyst, Cantor

briefings.tldr: Property and casualty (P&C) insurance is currently experiencing a generational personal lines soft market and a transition to a commercial lines soft market, with Ryan Tunis advising caution on personal lines due to ADAS-driven accident rate drops while highlighting AIG and Travelers as top commercial picks.

briefings.title: The AI Trade, Rising Rates, and Why the Market Is Still Standing | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 73
briefings.tldr: Despite a tumultuous mid-year environment marked by geopolitical conflict, rising interest rates, and massive AI capital expenditures, the U.S. stock market has proven remarkably resilient due to strong economic growth, robust underlying market internals, and a highly rotational tape.

briefings.title: Private Credit's Clock is Ticking w/ Glenn Schorr & Ken Worthington | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 72
briefings.tldr: Steve Eisman, joined by Glenn Schorr of Evercore and Ken Worthington of JP Morgan, explores the looming refinancing crunch in private credit software loans, the mechanics of retail broker cash yield optimization via agentic AI, crypto use cases versus Bitcoin’s store-of-value thesis, and a booming second-quarter earnings season for major investment banks.

briefings.title: 250 Years of American Capitalism: Hamilton, the GFC, & the AI Boom | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 71
briefings.tldr: In a sweeping retrospective on 250 years of U.S. economic history, Steve Eisman and co-author Adrian Wooldridge analyze how American capitalism evolved from the Hamilton-Jefferson debate through the Industrial Revolution, Great Depression, and Great Financial Crisis, driven by a unique national culture of entrepreneurial ambition and corporate innovation.

briefings.title: AI Revolution: Winners & Losers w/ Dan Ives & Gil Luria | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 70
briefings.tldr: The AI trade has evolved from an uncritical consensus into a complex debate over return on investment (ROI), capital intensity, and software disruption, with Dan Ives remaining firmly bullish on the structural buildout while Gil Luria advocates for a nuanced, stock-by-stock approach to identify emerging winners and losers.

briefings.title: AI Dominates Economy and Markets with Torsten Slok | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 68
briefings.tldr: The U.S. economy is currently buoyed by three non-interest-rate-sensitive "tailwinds"—AI spending, re-industrialization, and tax refunds—which are masking a severe K-shaped divergence and preventing the Federal Reserve from cutting rates.

briefings.title: Who Wins the Midterms & What It Means for Markets with Dan Clifton | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 67
briefings.tldr: The 2026 midterm elections are trending toward a split government with Democrats favored to flip the House, while the Federal Reserve prepares for a "regime change" under Kevin Warsh focused on shrinking the $6 trillion balance sheet rather than immediate rate cuts.

briefings.title: The Market's Biggest Warning Signs Right Now with Todd Sohn | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 66
briefings.tldr: The US stock market is experiencing historic concentration, with technology and semiconductors dominating the S&P 500 and capturing $27 billion in flows since March 30, while all other sectors saw net outflows.

briefings.title: The Real State of the American Consumer w/ Three Evercore Analysts | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 65
briefings.tldr: The K-shaped recovery is evolving into a "limping" middle class, forcing a mass consumer migration away from high-priced fast food and legacy carb-heavy brands toward value-driven platforms like Walmart.

briefings.title: Is Private Equity Destroying the Life Insurance Industry? | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 64
briefings.tldr: While private equity (PE) firms assume more illiquidity and concentration risk than traditional life insurers to harvest an extra 100 basis points of yield, they are not taking reckless credit risks.

briefings.title: The AI Semiconductor Boom and What Could End It with Stacy Rasgon | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 63
briefings.tldr: The semiconductor sector has transitioned from a niche AI boom into a broad infrastructure super-cycle, with growth now shifting toward "bottlenecks" like memory and CPUs as AI evolves from content generation to autonomous "agentic" tasks.

briefings.title: The AI All-You-Can-Eat Buffet Is Ending with Gary Marcus | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 62
briefings.tldr: The massive wave of artificial intelligence capital expenditure is hitting a structural wall as Large Language Models (LLMs) reach scaling limits and fail to eliminate hallucinations.

briefings.title: How Silicon Valley Took Over the Defense Industry with Peter Arment | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 61
briefings.tldr: The U.S. defense sector is undergoing a massive shift as $66 billion in venture capital disrupts an over-consolidated, slow-moving military-industrial complex, while a parallel nuclear renaissance is driving overlooked growth for specialty suppliers.

briefings.title: FICO’s Monopoly is Fading & Consumers Are the Winners w/ Kelsey Zhu | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 59
briefings.tldr: FICO’s aggressive price hikes—increasing mortgage credit score costs from $0.60 to $10.00 per pull since 2022—have triggered a regulatory and competitive backlash that is ending its decades-long monopoly in favor of a duopoly with the lower-cost VantageScore.

briefings.title: Is a Market Melt-Up Coming? Why Tech & Semis Are Dominating Again | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 58
briefings.tldr: Despite recent geopolitical volatility, market leadership has rapidly reverted to AI, semiconductors, and power-related industrials, suggesting a potential 1999-style "melt-up" rather than a fundamental regime change.

briefings.title: Apollo's Private Credit Exposure: Chris Edson Weighs In | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 57

people.name: Chris Edson
people.role: Partner and Global Head of Originations, Apollo

briefings.tldr: Chris Edson (Apollo) argues that the "private credit panic" is overblown by clarifying that the $40 trillion industry extends far beyond risky software buyouts into diversified, asset-backed lending, where Apollo maintains low software exposure and high capital alignment.

briefings.title: John Spencer on What the Headlines Get Wrong About the Iran War | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 55
briefings.tldr: The United States and Israel have achieved unprecedented military success in "Operation Epic Fury," systematically dismantling Iran’s leadership and military infrastructure through a historic decapitation strike and high-precision warfare.

briefings.title: Catching a Falling Knife: The Truth About Software Stocks Today | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 54
briefings.tldr: The software sector is facing a massive valuation reset as generative AI threatens to dismantle traditional moats by lowering the cost of code creation and disrupting seat-based revenue models.

briefings.title: Is Private Credit the Next Systemic Crisis? Steve Liesman Weighs In | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 53
briefings.tldr: While the U.S. economy demonstrates "unforecastable resilience," the combination of opaque private credit markets, potential oil "stock" shocks, and political gridlock at the Federal Reserve creates a high-uncertainty environment that disproportionately threatens lower-income consumers.

briefings.title: Inside the Iran War with Steven Cook: What’s REALLY Happening? | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 52
briefings.tldr: The U.S. and Israel have achieved significant tactical successes in degrading Iran’s military and nuclear capabilities, but the strategic outcome remains highly uncertain as President Trump maintains vague war aims to preserve negotiation leverage.

briefings.title: The Only Health Insurance Stock You Can Own with Michael Ha | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 51
briefings.tldr: The once-stable health insurance sector is undergoing a structural crisis as government regulatory changes to "risk adjustment" models and Medicaid redeterminations erode profit margins for giants like UnitedHealth and Molina, revealing that massive vertical integration has failed to create operational efficiency.

briefings.title: Mark Cuban on the Broken Drug Pricing System & How PBMs Really Work | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 50
briefings.tldr: Mark Cuban is disrupting the $4 trillion U.S. healthcare industry by bypassing the opaque Pharmacy Benefit Manager (PBM) system to provide transparent, "Cost Plus 15%" pricing.

briefings.title: The Next Financial Crisis? Private Equity, Private Credit & Life Insurance | Real Eisman Playbook
briefings.tldr: The U.S. life insurance and annuity industry is facing a systemic "slow-boil" crisis driven by private equity giants using policyholder premiums to fund high-risk private credits while hiding massive leverage in opaque offshore "secret captives."

briefings.title: George Noble on Gold’s Rise, Crypto Doubts & Tesla’s Struggles | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 47
briefings.tldr: George Noble argues for a massive rotation out of overextended technology and "failed" crypto assets into reflationary sectors like energy and precious metals, citing extreme fiscal debasement and a looming AI "spectacular bust."

briefings.title: Daniel Guetta on the Guts of AI, Agentic AI & Why LLMs Hallucinate | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 46
briefings.tldr: While Large Language Models (LLMs) are "statistical parrots" that lack human-style reasoning, their ability to navigate unstructured data and act as "agentic" tools provides immense corporate value today, regardless of whether the technology ever achieves human-level superintelligence.
